```{r setup, include=FALSE}
knitr::opts_chunk$set(echo = TRUE)
```

```{r}
#Performance Rating Prediction using Classification Decision Tree.

#Understanding the employee_performance data.
myData <- read.csv("data/employee_performance.csv")

head(myData)

summary(myData) #From summary, their are no null or missing value!

str(myData)

#Making sure that their are no missing value
colSums(is.na(myData)) #Confirmed that their are no missing value!

#Now our Data is all set to predict performance rating!
```

```{r}
#Performance Rating distribution
table(myData$PerformanceRating)

barplot(table(myData$PerformanceRating),
        main = "Performance Rating Distribution",
        xlab = "Performance Rating",
        ylab = "Number of Employees",
        col = "lightgreen")

#This shows whether most employees are Normal(0) or High(1) performers.
```

```{r}
#Creating Boxplot for importance variables 
#Satisfaction score vs Performance Rating
boxplot(SatisfactionScore ~ PerformanceRating,
        data = myData,
        main = "Satisfaction Score by Performance Rating",
        xlab = "Performance Rating",
        ylab = "Satisfaction Score",
        col = "lightblue")


#Leadership Score vs Performance Rating
boxplot(LeadershipScore ~ PerformanceRating,
        data = myData,
        main = "Leadership Score by Performance Rating",
        xlab = "Performance Rating",
        ylab = "Leadership Score",
        col = "lightyellow")

#Number of Projects vs Performance Rating
boxplot(NumProjects ~ PerformanceRating,
        data = myData,
        main = "Number of Projects by Performance Rating",
        xlab = "Performance Rating",
        ylab = "Number of Projects",
        col = "lightpink")

#Training Hours vs Performance Rating
boxplot(TrainingHours ~ PerformanceRating,
        data = myData,
        main = "Training Hours by Performance Rating",
        xlab = "Performance Rating",
        ylab = "Training Hours",
        col = "plum1")
```

```{r}

#Splitting data into training and testing.
set.seed(123)

library(caret)
trainIndex <- createDataPartition(myData$PerformanceRating,
                                  p = 0.80,
                                  list = FALSE)

train_data <- myData[trainIndex, ]
test_data <- myData[-trainIndex, ]

#Training contain 80% of data and 20% for Testing.
nrow(train_data)
nrow(test_data)
```

```{r}
#Classification decision tree model.
library(rpart)
tree_model <- rpart(PerformanceRating ~ Age + EducationLevel + Department +
                      YearsExperience + WorkHoursPerWeek + Overtime +
                      NumProjects + TrainingHours + SatisfactionScore +
                      PromotionLast3Years + LeadershipScore,
                    data = train_data,
                    method = "class")

summary(tree_model)

library(rattle)
fancyRpartPlot(tree_model,
           main = "Decision Tree for Predicting Performance Rating")
```

```{r}

predictions <- predict(tree_model,
                       newdata = test_data,
                       type = "class")
head(predictions)
```

```{r}
#Confusion Matrix
test_data$Performance.Rating <- factor(test_data$PerformanceRating,
                                       levels = c("0","1"))

predictions <- factor(predictions,
                      levels = c("0","1"))

confusionMatrix(predictions, test_data$Performance.Rating)

#shows how well your model predicted Normal vs High performance.
```

```{r}
#Variable importance
tree_model$variable.importance

importance_df <- data.frame(
  Variable = names(tree_model$variable.importance),
  Importance = tree_model$variable.importance
)

importance_df

barplot(importance_df$Importance,
        names.arg = importance_df$Variable,
        main = "Variable Importance for Performance Rating",
        xlab = "Variables",
        ylab = "Importance",
        las = 2,
        col = "chocolate")
```

```{r}
# Decision tree pruning using complexity parameter to prevent overfitting.
printcp(tree_model)
plotcp(tree_model)

#Choosing the best CP value.
best_cp <- tree_model$cptable[which.min(tree_model$cptable[, "xerror"]), "CP"]

pruned_tree <- prune(tree_model, cp = best_cp)

library(rpart.plot)
rpart.plot(pruned_tree,
           main = "Pruned Decision Tree for Performance Rating")

#Now predicting again using pruned tree.
pruned_predictions <- predict(pruned_tree,
                              newdata = test_data,
                              type = "class")

confusionMatrix(pruned_predictions, test_data$Performance.Rating)

```
